context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It is architected as a cloud-native platform adhering to strict EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Self-service users)
* Librarians/Catalogers (Inventory managers)
* Library Administrators (System configurers)
* Library Management System (LMS)
* EU Payment Gateway
* National Library Database

## Relationships
* Library Patrons to LMS via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 (OAuth2/OIDC)
* Librarians and Administrators to LMS via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 (MFA/RBAC)
* LMS to EU Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST with mTLS
* LMS to National Library Database via SOAP/REST over HTTPS with mTLS

## Technology Stack
* AWS Frankfurt (EU region) for cloud infrastructure ensuring EU-only data residency
* TLS 1.3 and mTLS for secure data in transit
* AES-256 for data at rest and field-level PII encryption
* OAuth2, OIDC, and RBAC for authentication and authorization
* GitOps (ArgoCD) for deployment pipelines and container management
* OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing and SLO tracking

## Rationale
This architecture uses an EU-region cloud deployment and strict encryption protocols to meet legal data residency mandates. Additionally, centralized API gateways, mTLS, and distributed tracing ensure the system achieves secure operations and satisfies the <800ms search performance requirement.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a scalable solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and offer self-service portals. It ensures strict EU data residency compliance and meets sub-800ms search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
* **Users:** Library Patrons, Librarians/Catalogers, Library Administrators
* **Gateways:** API Gateway (Kong/Envoy), EU Payment Gateway, National Library Database
* **Frontends:** Patron Portal (Next.js), Librarian Dashboard (React)
* **Core Services:** Search & Catalogue Service (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch), Circulation Service, Notification Service, Integration Service
* **Data & Messaging:** PostgreSQL with Read Replicas, Message Broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ)
* **Security & Infrastructure:** Identity Provider (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC), HashiCorp Vault, Service Mesh

## Relationships
* **Patron Portal & Librarian Dashboard** -> **API Gateway** via HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC tokens
* **API Gateway** -> **Search & Catalogue Service** via gRPC with mTLS
* **Circulation Service, Notification Service, & Integration Service** <-> **Message Broker** via AMQP
* **Integration Service** -> **EU Payment Gateway & National Library Database** via REST with circuit breakers
* **Services** -> **PostgreSQL & Elasticsearch** via TLS 1.3 and mTLS within EU availability zones

## Technology Stack
* **Frontend:** Next.js (Patron Portal) and React (Librarian Dashboard) for role-optimized UI bundles
* **Backend & API:** Node.js/Go (Circulation), Python/Go (Integration), Kong/Envoy (API Gateway)
* **Search & Database:** Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (Search & Catalogue), PostgreSQL with Read Replicas (Transactional storage)
* **Messaging & Security:** Kafka/RabbitMQ (Message Broker), HashiCorp Vault (Secrets), OAuth 2.0 / OIDC (AuthN/AuthZ)
* **Infrastructure:** Terraform, OpenTelemetry, TLS 1.3, and AES-256 for EU-only compliance

## Rationale
This microservices-based C4 architecture isolates resource-heavy components like the Search & Catalogue Service to consistently achieve the <800ms performance SLA. Furthermore, it strictly enforces EU data residency through region-locked infrastructure and secures sensitive patron data using container isolation, mTLS, and GDPR-compliant PII masking.

Patron Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Patron Portal is a secure self-service web interface enabling library patrons to catalogue items, manage accounts, and handle circulation tasks. It ensures high performance and strictly adheres to EU-only data residency requirements.

## Key Elements
*   Library Patrons (Users)
*   Patron Portal Container (Next.js)
*   UI Presentation Layer (React / Tailwind CSS)
*   BFF / Route Handler Layer (Next.js Node.js runtime)
*   API Gateway (Kong / Envoy)
*   EU Payment Gateway
*   EU-region CDN & Kubernetes Cluster

## Relationships
*   Library Patrons -> Patron Portal: Accesses self-service features [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
*   UI Presentation Layer -> BFF Layer: Internal React Server Actions [Direct IPC]
*   BFF Layer -> API Gateway: Proxied requests with injected OIDC tokens [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
*   API Gateway -> EU Payment Gateway: Processes fine payments [HTTPS]
*   EU CDN -> Patron Portal Container: Serves cached static assets and edge traffic [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
*   Next.js (React/Tailwind CSS): Powers server-rendered UI and BFF components for performance and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility.
*   OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Manages secure authentication with tokens stored exclusively in BFF server memory.
*   Kubernetes & EU CDN: Deploys container workloads locally to enforce EU data residency and <800ms search SLAs.
*   TLS 1.3: Secures all data in transit across system boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern to isolate sensitive session tokens and enforce strict security controls without degrading user experience. Deploying within an EU-region container cluster and CDN guarantees compliance with regional data residency constraints while meeting high-performance response SLAs.

Librarian Dashboard.analysis:
## Overview
The Librarian Dashboard is a secure, high-performance React-based Single Page Application (SPA) providing library staff with tools for catalog management, circulation, and administrative analytics. It connects exclusively via an API Gateway to backend microservices while adhering to strict EU data residency requirements.

## Key Elements
- Librarian Dashboard (React SPA container)
- Authentication Wrapper (React Context / OIDC Client component)
- Catalog Management Module (Lazy-loaded React component)
- Circulation & Overdue Handler (React component)
- Analytics & Admin Console (React component)
- API Client Layer (Axios/Fetch wrapper component)
- State & Routing Management (React Router & Zustand/Context)
- API Gateway (Kong/Envoy)

## Relationships
- Librarians, Catalogers, and Library Administrators -> Librarian Dashboard: Manages catalog, circulation, and configurations [HTTPS]
- Librarian Dashboard -> API Gateway: Makes API requests with short-lived tokens and idempotency headers [HTTPS (REST/GraphQL)]
- Librarian Dashboard -> EU-restricted CDN (e.g., AWS CloudFront): Serves static immutable assets [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- React: Powers the component-based user interface for rapid bundle optimization
- OAuth 2.0 / OIDC: Secures user sessions with in-memory token storage
- Zustand / React Router: Manages local application state and role-based route guards
- Axios / Fetch: Handles API requests with centralized error handling and exponential backoff retry logic
- AWS CloudFront (EU edge-node restricted): Deploys static SPA assets to satisfy data residency constraints

## Rationale
The component-based React architecture ensures rapid, lazy-loaded workflow efficiency and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility for power users. Deploying via an EU-restricted CDN with in-memory token handling and strict API Gateway integration fulfills regional data protection mandates and sub-second performance goals.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform for public and academic libraries designed to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- **Users:** Library Patrons, Librarians/Catalogers, Library Administrators
- **Frontends:** Patron Portal (Next.js), Librarian Dashboard (React)
- **API Gateway Layer:** Envoy Proxy (handling routing, rate-limiting, and ingress security)
- **Core Services:** Search & Catalogue Service (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch), Circulation Service (Node.js/Go), Notification Service (Node.js/Go), Integration Service (Python/Go)
- **Infrastructure & Security:** HashiCorp Vault, Message Broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ), PostgreSQL Database, Identity Provider (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC)
- **External Systems:** EU Payment Gateway, National Library Database

## Relationships
- Patron Portal -> API Gateway: Makes HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) API requests with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC tokens
- Librarian Dashboard -> API Gateway: Makes HTTPS (REST/GraphQL) API requests with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC tokens
- API Gateway -> Search & Catalogue Service: Queries catalogue via gRPC with mTLS
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider: Offloads token validation and claim verification
- Envoy Proxy -> HashiCorp Vault: Automates short-lived mTLS certificate rotation

## Technology Stack
- **API Gateway:** Envoy Proxy configured via xDS dynamic control planes and WebAssembly (Wasm) filters for robust performance, gRPC-web support, and low memory footprint
- **Frontend:** Next.js (Patron Portal) and React (Librarian Dashboard)
- **Search:** Elasticsearch/OpenSearch to satisfy the <800ms search NFR
- **Security & Auth:** OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, HashiCorp Vault, TLS 1.3 ingress, and mTLS internal transport
- **Observability:** Prometheus/OpenTelemetry with W3C Trace Context propagation restricted to EU backends

## Rationale
This architecture uses Envoy Proxy to establish a secure, observable trust boundary that successfully isolates public traffic while enforcing EU data residency constraints. The decoupled microservices and circuit-breaking modules guarantee high performance and sub-800ms search responses under peak loads.

Search & Catalogue Service.analysis:
## Overview
- Search & Catalogue Service for the Library Management System, providing high-performance item discovery and cataloging.
- Built to handle multi-format physical and digital assets while strictly enforcing EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Search API Controller (Go, Gin/gRPC)
- Catalog Management Engine (Python, FastAPI)
- Search Index Client (OpenSearch wrapper with Facet Configuration Component)
- Analytics & Logging Collector (Async Worker)
- OpenSearch Cluster (StatefulSet, EU-localized Persistent Volumes)
- HashiCorp Vault (Secret Management)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Search API Controller: Queries catalogue via gRPC with mTLS
- Search API Controller -> Search Index Client: Executes search queries via OpenSearch REST API over TLS 1.3
- Catalog Management Engine -> Search Index Client: Synchronizes metadata updates via OpenSearch Bulk API over TLS 1.3
- Search API Controller -> Analytics & Logging Collector: Offloads anonymized query metrics via Kafka/RabbitMQ
- Internal Components -> HashiCorp Vault: Dynamic secret injection via HashiCorp Vault sidecars

## Technology Stack
- Go (Gin/gRPC): Selected for the Search API Controller to ensure high-throughput, low-latency search query handling.
- Python (FastAPI): Chosen for the Catalog Management Engine to efficiently handle complex metadata ingestion and synchronization.
- OpenSearch: Implemented for multi-format indexing, faceting, and relevance scoring, compliant with EU-only data residency constraints.
- Kubernetes StatefulSet: Used for stateful OpenSearch deployment with regional EU anti-affinity rules.
- HashiCorp Vault: Utilized for secure, dynamic credential management and TDE encryption keys.

## Rationale
- Decomposing the service into independent read (Search API) and write (Catalog Engine) components enables isolated horizontal autoscaling for peak loads.
- Asynchronous analytics offloading and strict mTLS/JWT security boundaries protect the 99th-percentile <800ms search latency SLA (R-05) and EU compliance mandates.
Search & Catalogue Service.yaml_definition:
level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Search & Catalogue Service container"
parentContainer:
  name: "Search & Catalogue Service"
elements:
  - type: "component"

Circulation Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Circulation Service is a high-throughput microservice managing library loans, renewals, and returns within the Library Management System. It ensures zero-downtime transactions and strict EU data residency compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Loan API Controller**: REST/gRPC endpoints validating incoming JWTs from the API Gateway and enforcing RBAC.
- **Loan Domain Engine**: Core business logic handling checkouts, renewals, returns, and grace periods.
- **Circulation Repository & Outbox Store**: Data access layer managing transactional state and reliable event publishing.
- **Event Publisher/Subscriber**: Asynchronous message handler interfacing with the message broker.
- **PostgreSQL Database**: Persistent transactional store utilizing read replicas.
- **HashiCorp Vault**: Dynamic secrets and encryption key manager.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> Loan API Controller**: Forwards authenticated requests via JWT/OAuth 2.0.
- **Loan Domain Engine -> Circulation Repository**: Executes transactional reads/writes.
- **Circulation Repository -> PostgreSQL Database**: Persists data securely via TLS 1.3 and mTLS.
- **Event Publisher -> Message Broker**: Publishes domain events using AMQP with the Outbox Pattern.
- **Circulation Service -> HashiCorp Vault**: Fetches dynamic secrets via Kubernetes Service Account token exchange.

## Technology Stack
- **Go (Golang)**: Chosen for high throughput, concurrency model, and low memory footprint.
- **pgx Driver**: PostgreSQL driver enforcing TLS 1.3, connection pooling, and resilient data access.
- **Kubernetes**: Container orchestration platform for horizontal scaling, probes, and resource governance.
- **OpenTelemetry & Prometheus**: Observability stacks for distributed tracing, metrics, and outbox lag monitoring.

## Rationale
Decomposing the Circulation Service into strict internal components using Go guarantees high-performance self-service availability. The Outbox Pattern and decoupled event publishing ensure transactional resilience during peak workloads while maintaining EU compliance.

Notification Service.analysis:
## Overview
[Library Management System] is a public and academic library solution designed for cataloging items, managing circulation, and providing self-service portals with strict EU data residency.

## Key Elements
- Notification Service (Node.js/Go container)
- Event Consumer Component (Go)
- Preference & Template Engine (Node.js/Go)
- Dispatch Adapter Component (Go)
- Audit & Logging Component (Go)
- Message Broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ)
- PostgreSQL Database
- HashiCorp Vault
- External EU-hosted Email/SMS Providers

## Relationships
- Event Consumer -> Message Broker: Consumes domain events [AMQP/mTLS]
- Preference & Template Engine -> PostgreSQL Database: Queries preferences and opt-out flags [SQL/TLS]
- Dispatch Adapter -> HashiCorp Vault: Fetches provider secrets [HTTPS/Token Auth with AppRole]
- Dispatch Adapter -> External Email/SMS Providers: Sends notifications [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Dispatch Adapter -> Audit & Logging Component: Records delivery timestamps [In-memory/gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Go & Node.js: Selected for asynchronous workload handling and micro-component performance.
- HashiCorp Vault: Used with AppRole authentication for dynamic credential management.
- PostgreSQL Database: Stores anonymized delivery logs and patron channel preferences.
- Message Broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ): Provides asynchronous queuing, dead-letter queues (DLQs), and backpressure control.
- OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Enables distributed tracing, queue lag monitoring, and metric alerting.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures secure, asynchronous multi-channel notification delivery while strictly adhering to GDPR and EU-only data residency requirements. Decoupling components and isolating PII support reliable patron engagement, zero-downtime scalability, and effective librarian dispute resolution.

Integration Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Integration Service coordinates external third-party communication for the Library Management System. It ensures secure, resilient data exchange while strictly enforcing EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Integration Service (Container)
- API Client Component (Go SDK)
- Message Consumer/Producer Component
- Synchronization Orchestrator
- Idempotency Manager Component
- External: EU Payment Gateway, National Library Database
- External: Message Broker (Kafka/RabbitMQ), HashiCorp Vault

## Relationships
- Integration Service -> Message Broker: Publishes and consumes messages [AMQP with mTLS]
- Integration Service -> EU Payment Gateway: Processes payments and webhooks [REST over TLS 1.3 with circuit breakers]
- Integration Service -> National Library Database: Synchronizes library records [REST over TLS 1.3 with rate limiting]
- Integration Service -> HashiCorp Vault: Dynamically fetches runtime credentials [REST via short-lived tokens]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for lightweight concurrency, fast startup times, and low-level protocol control
- HashiCorp Vault: Provides dynamic secret injection and eliminates local credential storage
- OpenTelemetry: Enables end-to-end distributed tracing across internal events and external APIs
- Redis: Powers the internal Idempotency Manager to prevent duplicate transactions
- Kubernetes: Hosts the containerized service with Horizontal Pod Autoscalers driven by consumer lag

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict EU data residency and robust security through mTLS, TLS 1.3, and container hardening. It maintains high availability and protects downstream services via circuit breakers, asynchronous retry queues, and idempotency management.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The system ensures EU-only data residency and sub-800ms search responses.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Library Patrons, Librarians/Catalogers, Library Administrators
- **External Systems**: EU Payment Gateway, National Library Database
- **Containers**: Patron Portal (Next.js), Librarian Dashboard (React), API Gateway (Kong/Envoy), Search & Catalogue Service (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch), Circulation Service (Node.js/Go), Notification Service (Node.js/Go), Integration Service (Python/Go), Message Broker (RabbitMQ), PostgreSQL Database (PostgreSQL with Read Replicas), Identity Provider (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC), HashiCorp Vault
- **Components (Message Broker)**: Exchange Routing Engine, Queue Manager, Consumer Delivery Manager, Dead-Letter Routing & Policy Engine, Access Control & TLS Termination Proxy

## Relationships
- Patron Portal -> API Gateway: HTTPS/REST [JSON]
- Librarian Dashboard -> API Gateway: HTTPS/REST [JSON]
- Circulation Service -> Message Broker: Publishes/consumes events [AMQP 0-9-1 via TLS 1.3]
- Notification Service -> Message Broker: Consumes events [AMQP 0-9-1 via TLS 1.3]
- Integration Service -> Message Broker: Publishes/consumes events [AMQP 0-9-1 via TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- RabbitMQ: Chosen for flexible AMQP routing, per-queue dead-lettering, and fine-grained topic ACLs
- HashiCorp Vault: Provides dynamic credential generation and application-layer payload encryption for PII
- TLS 1.3 & mTLS: Enforces strict transport security and service authentication
- Kubernetes: EU-hosted clustered deployment for high availability and quorum queues

## Rationale
This architecture uses RabbitMQ with mirrored quorum queues across EU zones to guarantee zero data loss, sub-2-second event delivery, and strict GDPR compliance. Security controls like mTLS, Vault-backed encryption, and ACLs protect sensitive patron data without compromising performance.

PostgreSQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service patron portals. The system ensures robust data protection, high availability, and strict adherence to EU data residency mandates.

## Key Elements
- **Circulation Service & Search Service**: Microservices handling patron transactions, item checkouts, and catalogue searches.
- **Connection Pooler (PgBouncer)**: Manages incoming database connections and terminates mTLS.
- **Primary Transaction Engine (PostgreSQL Primary)**: Handles all write operations, enforcing Row-Level Security and `pgaudit` logging.
- **Read Replica Instances (PostgreSQL Replicas)**: Offloads read-heavy operations and hosts the dedicated Reporting & Analytics Schema.
- **HashiCorp Vault**: Manages dynamic database credentials and Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) keys.
- **DevOps & Monitoring Stack**: CloudNativePG operator, Prometheus (`postgres_exporter`), Grafana, and automated WAL-shipping to S3-compatible EU storage.

## Relationships
- Circulation Service / Search Service -> Connection Pooler: Routes queries via TCP / TLS 1.3
- Connection Pooler -> Primary Transaction Engine: Proxies write operations via TCP with inner-node TLS 1.3
- Connection Pooler -> Read Replica Instances: Routes read-only reports via TCP with inner-node TLS 1.3
- Primary Transaction Engine -> High-Availability Standby: Synchronizes state via WAL-shipping (Streaming Replication)
- PostgreSQL Replicas -> Reporting & Analytics Schema: Serves isolated analytical queries for Library Administrators

## Technology Stack
- **Database**: PostgreSQL with Read Replicas for scalable transactional and analytical isolation.
- **Connection Pooling**: PgBouncer to prevent connection exhaustion during peak loads.
- **Encryption & Secrets**: HashiCorp Vault for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and dynamic credential rotation.
- **Compliance & Auditing**: PostgreSQL `pgaudit` extension for SIEM logging.
- **Infrastructure & Deployment**: Kubernetes with CloudNativePG operator, Flyway/Liquibase for zero-downtime schema migrations.
- **Observability**: Prometheus (`postgres_exporter`) and Grafana routed to PagerDuty.

## Rationale
This architecture fits the requirements by isolating analytical reporting on read replicas to maintain <800ms search and transaction performance. Furthermore, private subnet deployment, mTLS, Vault-managed encryption, and automated EU-region backups guarantee strict compliance with EU data residency and security mandates.

Identity Provider.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. Its Identity Provider ensures secure, EU-compliant authentication and authorization.

## Key Elements
- **Identity Provider (Keycloak / Java/Quarkus)**: Core container managing authentication, authorization, and sessions.
- **Authentication Engine**: Handles OIDC/OAuth2 protocols and PKCE.
- **User Management & RBAC Service**: Manages profiles and maps roles to JWT claims.
- **Session & Token Management Service**: Manages active user sessions and token revocation.
- **Adaptive MFA & Policy Engine**: Evaluates risk signals for step-up authentication.
- **Federation & JIT Provisioning Component**: Manages external IdPs (Google, Shibboleth SAML).
- **UI & Localization Component**: Renders multi-language login and consent pages.
- **HashiCorp Vault**: Stores cryptographic key material.
- **PostgreSQL Database**: Persists identity state.

## Relationships
- Patron Portal / Librarian Dashboard to Authentication Engine via HTTPS (OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE)
- Session & Token Management Service to HashiCorp Vault via HTTPS/REST (Transit Secrets Engine)
- Identity Provider containers to PostgreSQL Database via JDBC (TLS)
- Inter-node session replication via Infinispan (ENCRYPT_TCP)

## Technology Stack
- **Keycloak (Java/Quarkus)**: Chosen for robust OIDC support, extensibility, and enterprise federation features.
- **HashiCorp Vault**: Selected for secure, centralized cryptographic key management and rotation.
- **Infinispan**: Used for distributed session clustering and replication across Keycloak replicas.
- **PostgreSQL**: Chosen for reliable, ACID-compliant relational data storage within the EU boundary.
- **OAuth 2.0 / OIDC / SAML 2.0**: Protocols enforcing open standards for federation and token exchange.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU data residency and low-latency token validation by keeping all identity services and data strictly localized. Clustered Keycloak containers with Infinispan provide high availability and fault tolerance for user sessions.

HashiCorp Vault.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Library Management System]
[Core Purpose: Catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals with strict EU data residency.]

## Key Elements
- HashiCorp Vault (Secrets Management)
- Integrated Raft Storage Backend
- Core/HTTP API Layer
- Vault Agent Sidecar (Component)
- Circulation Service, Integration Service, Next.js Patron Portal, React Librarian Dashboard
- PostgreSQL Database with Read Replicas
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch (Search & Catalogue)
- Kong/Envoy API Gateway

## Relationships
- Circulation/Integration Services communicate with Vault Agent Sidecar via HTTP over Unix Domain Sockets / localhost TCP
- Vault Agent Sidecar communicates with Core/HTTP API Layer via HTTPS (REST) over mTLS (Port 8200)
- Core/HTTP API Layer persists encrypted data to Integrated Raft Storage Backend using Raft internal RPC over TLS
- API Gateway routes external traffic to Patron/Librarian frontends and backend services

## Technology Stack
- HashiCorp Vault with Integrated Raft: High availability, zero external data residency leaks
- Vault Agent Sidecar: Client-side caching and transit security
- PostgreSQL & Elasticsearch: Core persistence and sub-800ms search performance
- Kubernetes & Helm: Deployment and orchestration
- TLS 1.3 & mTLS: Transit security and encryption

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies EU data residency constraints through localized Raft storage and regional Cloud KMS auto-unseal mechanisms.]
[Vault Agent sidecars and Database Secrets Engines ensure sub-second patron checkouts, high availability (99.99%), and dynamic credential security without operational friction.]
